prompt.context_jp: 岡田が梅本副市長の経緯を説明している。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「梅本さん___ それを裏切って 出馬したんですね」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that introduces Umemoto as the one who did the betraying.

feedback.correct_en: Kiyomi is naming Umemoto as the identified actor behind a surprising event just revealed — 'it was Umemoto who betrayed him.' That exhaustive/new-information role is marked by が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would turn Umemoto into a known topic, flattening the 'aha, so SHE's the one' feel that fits this reveal. を doesn't fit a subject slot.

contrast_examples.en: (As for the culprit,) it's him. — topic は
HE is the culprit. — identifying が

prompt.context_jp: 梅本の立候補を知った古屋氏の反応について。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「もちろん 古屋さん___寝耳に水だから大激怒で」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that frames Furuya as the topic whose reaction we're describing.

feedback.correct_en: Furuya has already been introduced as the former mayor; now the speaker comments on his reaction. That 'as for Furuya, …' topic frame uses は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would re-introduce him as new information, which is odd when he's the shared referent. に doesn't fit this slot.

contrast_examples.en: As for Furuya, he got angry.
It was Furuya who got angry.

prompt.context_jp: 1億円という価格を岡田が高いと言った直後。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「かなり高いです あそこの適正価格___ 6300万くらいなんで」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that sets the fair price against the 100-million figure.

feedback.correct_en: The sale price (1億) was just mentioned; now 'the fair price, by contrast, is about 63 million.' That contrastive framing wants は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would make 6300万 a brand-new identification, losing the explicit contrast with the 1億 just said. を can't mark the subject here.

contrast_examples.jp: 買値は1億、適正価格は6300万。
contrast_examples.en: The purchase price is 100M; the fair price (by contrast) is 63M.
It's 63M that is the fair price. (identifies, no contrast)

prompt.context_jp: 中本さんから送られた写真を見直しているところ。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「この写真 よく見たら 後ろに市長___写り込んでて」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for a new discovery visible in the photo.

feedback.correct_en: The mayor appearing in the background is fresh, surprising information noticed on close inspection — classic が for new-information presentation.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would treat 市長 as an already-established topic, which flattens the discovery. も would suggest 'the mayor TOO', implying someone else was already shown.

contrast_examples.en: Oh, there's a rainbow! (newly noticed — が)
Rainbows are pretty. (topic は)

prompt.context_jp: 幹部が二分化した話のあと、清美が岡田に尋ねる。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「ちなみに 岡田さん___ どっち派なんですか？」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for asking Okada about his own alignment.

feedback.correct_en: Okada is right there in the conversation; Kiyomi makes him the topic ('as for you, Mr. Okada, which side?'). That's は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would sound like identifying who among many is on some side — not the natural way to ask someone about themselves.

contrast_examples.en: What do YOU think? (topic は)
Who's in favor? (identifying が)

prompt.context_jp: 同僚が不正の疑いを岡田に相談している回想。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「部長___梅本派だからさ」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that frames the chief as the topic being characterized.

feedback.correct_en: The speaker is characterizing a known person (the chief) — 'as for the chief, he's on Umemoto's side.' That's topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn it into an identification ('it's the chief who is Umemoto-faction'), which doesn't match the explanatory tone with だから.

contrast_examples.en: My father is a doctor. (topic は)
The doctor is my father. (identifying が)

prompt.context_jp: 奥田支配人が事務所の見取り図を説明している。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「2階の階段を上った正面___ オーナーの部屋です」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for identifying exactly where the owner's room is.

feedback.correct_en: The manager is pinpointing the single spot that is the owner's room — exhaustive identification among possible rooms. が fits that 'X is where it is' feel.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would just comment on a known location, losing the pointing-out force needed for a floor-plan briefing.

contrast_examples.en: THIS is the entrance. (pinpointing — が)
The entrance is here. (as for the entrance… — は)

prompt.context_jp: ミノケンが解決策を提案する場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「いちばん手っとり早いの___ 合意書を見つけることかな」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that frames 'the quickest route' as the topic being described.

feedback.correct_en: 'The quickest way' is set up as the topic, and the predicate names what that way is. XはYだ 'as for X, it's Y' uses は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would create a presentational 'the quickest way exists / stands out', which doesn't match the defining XはYだ structure Minoken is using.

contrast_examples.en: My hobby is reading. (XはYだ — は)
Our tastes match. (が as subject)

prompt.context_jp: 岡田が古屋前市長を擁護している。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「まあ イメージ___悪いけど 不正とかも絶対にやらなかったし」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that sets 'image' against the positive point to follow.

feedback.correct_en: The けど flags a contrast: 'his image is bad, BUT he never cheated.' That contrastive は carves out one dimension while implying others differ.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would just report a neutral fact about his image, missing the 'yes-but' structure that the whole sentence is built on.

contrast_examples.jp: 見た目は悪いけど、味はいい。
contrast_examples.en: Looks bad, but tastes good. (contrastive は)
The looks are bad. (plain description — が)

prompt.context_jp: 古屋前市長の人物評を岡田が語る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「問題発言とかも多いけど…何だかんだで 市のこと___ ちゃんと考えてた人だったので」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that contrasts 'the city' against his flaws.

feedback.correct_en: After listing negatives, 市のこと is singled out as the one thing he DID care about — a contrastive singling-out that uses は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would turn 市のこと into a plain new subject, missing the 'at least this one thing' nuance set up by the preceding けど clause.

contrast_examples.jp: 勉強はしないけど、運動はする。
contrast_examples.en: Doesn't study, but DOES exercise. (contrastive は)
Likes exercise. (plain subject — が)

prompt.context_jp: 選挙前の梅本の動きについて。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「梅本さん___ 副市長時代に 後援会の人たちにも その辺の 根回しをやってたらしくて」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that keeps Umemoto as the ongoing topic.

feedback.correct_en: Umemoto has been the running topic for several lines. Continuing to comment on her uses は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would re-introduce her as if she were newly identified, which breaks the flow of ongoing discussion about her.

contrast_examples.en: He runs every morning. (habitual topic — は)
HE's the one running. (identifying — が)

prompt.context_jp: 同僚が資料を持ち出そうとした結果を岡田が語る。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「資料を持ち出そうと してんの___バレちゃって」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for the nominalized clause being discovered.

feedback.correct_en: The nominalized 'the fact he was trying to sneak documents out' is the subject of バレる (got found out). Subordinate/eventive subjects like this take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would elevate it to a sentence-level topic, which doesn't fit this inside-the-clause subject. を doesn't match バレる's intransitive frame.

contrast_examples.jp: 嘘をついたのがバレた。
contrast_examples.en: The fact that he lied was found out.
Lies are bad. (topic は)

prompt.context_jp: 鑑定書への岡田の疑念。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「その鑑定書も 梅本さんの息のかかった鑑定士___ 出したものだと思うんですよ」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle that marks the subject inside the relative clause.

feedback.correct_en: Inside a relative clause ('[the one that] an appraiser tied to Umemoto issued'), the subject takes が, not は.
feedback.incorrect_en: は generally can't live inside a relative clause this way — it belongs at the main-clause topic level.

contrast_examples.en: The book he wrote. (が in relative clause)
He wrote a book. (は in main clause)

prompt.context_jp: 清美が梅本市長について尋ねた直後の岡田の返答。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「あの人___… 相当 キレ者ですね」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for commenting on 'that person' as the topic.

feedback.correct_en: Kiyomi just asked about 梅本さん, so あの人 is a known referent. Making a characterization about her ('she's shrewd') uses topic は.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would be an identifying answer like 'SHE's the shrewd one', which doesn't match an open 'what kind of person is she?' question.

contrast_examples.en: That person is kind. (topic は)
THAT person is the culprit. (identifying が)

prompt.context_jp: 高橋がみずぽんのスマホに保護フィルムを貼ってくれた話。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「あれ お店___ 1000円ぐらいしちゃうもんね」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the particle for 'at a shop' as the setting of the implied transaction.

feedback.correct_en: だと sets up a hypothetical frame — 'if it were a shop, it'd cost about 1000 yen.' That's the natural pairing with しちゃう here.
feedback.incorrect_en: には marks a destination/recipient, not a hypothetical scenario. から would mean 'from a shop'.

contrast_examples.en: At a convenience store, it's expensive.

contrast_examples.jp: コンビニから電話する。
contrast_examples.en: I'll call from the convenience store.

prompt.context_jp: 署名運動では難しいと言われた清美の反応。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「梅本さん___ 話くらい聞いてもらえるかなと 思ってたんですけど」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the form that means 'if it's Umemoto (of all people)'.

feedback.correct_en: なら sets up 'if it's X / in X's case', which fits Kiyomi's hopeful 'surely Umemoto, of all people, would at least listen.'
feedback.incorrect_en: から would mean 'because of Umemoto', and には would misframe her as a destination, losing the conditional reasoning.

contrast_examples.en: If it's him, he should get it.
I heard it from him.

prompt.context_jp: 梅本の裏切りを知った古屋氏の反応。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「古屋さんは____だから大激怒で」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the set phrase meaning 'completely blindsided'.

feedback.correct_en: 寝耳に水 literally 'water in a sleeping ear' = a bolt from the blue. It fits a 'he had no idea it was coming and was furious' context.
feedback.incorrect_en: 焼け石に水 means 'drop in the bucket' (useless effort). 口から水 isn't an idiom.

contrast_examples.jp: その知らせは寝耳に水だった。
contrast_examples.en: The news was a bolt from the blue.

contrast_examples.jp: 今さら謝っても焼け石に水だ。
contrast_examples.en: Apologizing now is a drop in the bucket.

prompt.context_jp: 梅本が選挙前に後援会にしていたこと。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「後援会の人たちにも その辺の ____をやってたらしくて」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word for 'behind-the-scenes groundwork'.

feedback.correct_en: 根回し is the standard term for pre-arranging support behind the scenes before making a move public — exactly what Umemoto did with the kōenkai.
feedback.incorrect_en: 手回し means 'preparation/arrangement' more generally, not political groundwork. 気配り is 'consideration/attentiveness', not maneuvering.

contrast_examples.jp: 事前に根回ししておく。
contrast_examples.en: Lay the groundwork beforehand.
Well-prepared / quick on the draw.

prompt.context_jp: 岡田が予算委員会の結果を予想していた場面。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「さすがに予算委員会で ____されるんじゃないかと思って」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the verb for a committee 'voting it down'.

feedback.correct_en: 否決される = 'be voted down/rejected', which fits Okada's expectation that the inflated price would be struck down.
feedback.incorrect_en: 採決 is 'taking a vote' (the act, not the outcome). 解決 is 'resolution/solving a problem', not a vote outcome.

contrast_examples.en: The bill was voted down.
Put the bill to a vote.

prompt.context_jp: 岡田が梅本の動機を推測している。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「オーナーから個人的に ____を受け取るんだと思います」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the noun for an illicit kickback.

feedback.correct_en: 賄賂 is 'bribe' — the illegal payment at the heart of Okada's corruption theory.
feedback.incorrect_en: 謝礼 is a legitimate thank-you fee, and 寄付 is a donation. Neither carries the illegal nuance the story requires.

contrast_examples.en: Accept a bribe.
Pay an honorarium.

prompt.context_jp: ミノケンが打開策を提案する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「いちばん ____のは 合意書を見つけることかな」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the adjective meaning 'quickest / most straightforward'.

feedback.correct_en: 手っとり早い = 'quick and direct'. It fits Minoken offering the fastest route to proving the bribe.
feedback.incorrect_en: 気っ風がいい means 'generous-spirited' (about a person). 手厚い means 'generous/thorough in treatment' (e.g. support), not fast.

contrast_examples.jp: 手っとり早く説明する。
contrast_examples.en: Explain it quickly/concisely.
Entertain lavishly.

prompt.context_jp: 高橋が逆にチャンスだと言う理由。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「これがさ ____土地を買って 施設を建てるだけだったら どうにもできないけど」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the adverb meaning 'legitimately / above-board'.

feedback.correct_en: 真っ当に = 'properly / above-board'. Takahashi contrasts a legitimate purchase against the actual corrupt one.
feedback.incorrect_en: 真っ先に means 'first of all'. 真っ直ぐに means 'straight (direction/manner)', not 'legally'.

contrast_examples.en: Earn an honest living.
Raised my hand first of all.

prompt.context_jp: 葉月が暴き方のアイデアを出す。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「いやいや ____とかさ できないの？」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the noun for 'whistleblowing'.

feedback.correct_en: 内部告発 = 'whistleblowing': someone inside reports wrongdoing. That's exactly Hazuki's suggestion.
feedback.incorrect_en: 内部留保 is 'retained earnings' (finance). 内部監査 is 'internal audit' — a routine process, not a public exposé.

contrast_examples.jp: 内部告発で不正が発覚した。
contrast_examples.en: The fraud was exposed by a whistleblower.
Conduct an internal audit.

prompt.context_jp: 岡田が古屋前市長を評する。
prompt.prompt_jp: 「古屋さんって ____だし 問題発言とかも多いけど」
prompt.prompt_en: Pick the term meaning 'old-school / Showa-era mentality'.

feedback.correct_en: 昭和体質 characterizes a *way of being* stuck in Showa-era attitudes — fits a mayor making gaffes but caring old-school style.
feedback.incorrect_en: 昭和世代 just names a generation, not a mindset. 昭和記念 doesn't fit (it's part of a park name).

contrast_examples.jp: あの会社は昭和体質だ。
contrast_examples.en: That company has an old-school Showa mentality.
People of the Showa generation.

prompt.context_jp: 高橋が仲間たちに感謝を伝える、親しい内輪の場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which opener feels most natural for Takahashi's casual thank-you to close friends?

choices.text: なんか… ありがとね
このたびは誠にありがとうございます
ありがとうを申し上げます

feedback.correct_en: The scene is warm and informal — childhood-friend territory. なんか…ありがとね has the hesitant, affectionate tone that fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: このたびは誠に… is a stiff business opener that would sound bizarre among friends. ありがとうを申し上げます isn't even a natural collocation.

contrast_examples.en: Hey, uh, thanks. (friends)

contrast_examples.jp: このたびは誠にありがとうございます。
contrast_examples.en: Thank you very much on this occasion. (formal/business)

prompt.context_jp: 行く気のない相手にツッコむ、くだけた口語の場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which reply feels most natural when calling someone out for a vague 'I'll come if I can'?

choices.text: いや それ 来ないやつじゃない
それは参加されない方の表現です

feedback.correct_en: The ribbing tone 'that's what people say when they're NOT coming' is captured by casual '〜やつじゃない' + negative tag question. It matches the group's banter.
feedback.incorrect_en: The second option is stiff formal commentary and the third says the opposite of what Takahashi means.

contrast_examples.jp: それ、絶対来ないやつじゃん。
contrast_examples.en: That's a definite 'not coming' line, isn't it?

contrast_examples.jp: それは参加されない方の表現です。
contrast_examples.en: That is an expression used by non-attendees. (overly formal/robotic)

prompt.context_jp: 資料を撮りに行くと言う同僚を心配する場面。
prompt.prompt_en: Which reaction sounds most natural for a worried friend?

choices.text: ええっ？ 大丈夫？ 気をつけて
問題ないか確認願います
ご安全に作業されますように

feedback.correct_en: Short, in-the-moment worry calls for 大丈夫？気をつけて — exactly how a worried peer would react.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other options are business-memo or ceremonial phrasings that no close colleague would blurt out in alarm.

contrast_examples.en: You okay? Be careful. (natural concern)

contrast_examples.jp: ご安全に作業願います。
contrast_examples.en: Please operate safely. (industrial-notice style)

prompt.context_jp: 仲間内で梅本市長への怒りをぶちまける葉月のセリフ。
prompt.prompt_en: Which line fits Hazuki's blunt, among-friends outrage?

choices.text: マジで このばばあ 最悪だね
この御婦人には問題があるようです
当該市長殿におかれましては誠に遺憾でございます

feedback.correct_en: Hazuki is venting among childhood friends — マジで / ばばあ / 最悪 is the blunt casual register that matches her mood.
feedback.incorrect_en: The other two are polite/bureaucratic framings; using them while fuming over corruption would feel absurdly stiff.

contrast_examples.jp: マジで最悪なんだけど。
contrast_examples.en: Seriously the worst. (casual outrage)

contrast_examples.jp: 誠に遺憾でございます。
contrast_examples.en: We find it most regrettable. (official statement)

prompt.context_jp: オーナー原口が電話で共犯者に話しかける、礼儀正しい商談の口調。
prompt.prompt_en: Which opener fits Haraguchi's polite phone call to a conspirator?

choices.text: あっ もしもし 原口です 先ほどは どうも ありがとうございました
オス、原口だけど さっきマジ助かった
原口であらせられる。先刻は祝着至極

feedback.correct_en: On the surface Haraguchi plays the polite businessperson — もしもし + 先ほどは…ありがとうございました is the textbook phone-greeting register that matches.
feedback.incorrect_en: オス…マジ助かった is locker-room casual, wrong for a cover of politeness. The third is archaic/pseudo-classical and would never appear in a modern call.

contrast_examples.jp: もしもし、〇〇です。先日はありがとうございました。
contrast_examples.en: Hello, this is X. Thank you for the other day. (business phone)

contrast_examples.jp: オッス、俺。昨日サンキュな。
contrast_examples.en: Hey, it's me. Thanks for yesterday. (very casual)
